---
title: Walkthrough on a benchmark log
description: Load a Pier 4 driving record, build the capacity target, sweep the unlogged top segment, run the march, and propagate the uncertainty.
---

This example steps through the method on one of the benchmark piles,
pile B-20 of the Pier 4 data set. Each stage of `analyze`
is run by hand so that its inputs and outputs can be inspected. The
[method page](../user-guide/method.qmd) explains the equations behind
each stage.

## Load the record

The log is a CSV with one row per foot: toe elevation, hammer stroke and
blows per foot. This inspector recorded the stroke in feet instead of the
blow rate, so the `stroke` column is named; the package converts it to
blows per minute on input.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import driven_pile as dp

pile = dp.Pile.octagonal(width_in=24, length_ft=170.5)
hammer = dp.Hammer(ram_weight=20.0)  # kips

log = dp.DriveLog.from_csv(
    "data/B-20_log.csv",
    pile,
    hammer,
    elevation="elevation_ft",
    stroke="stroke_ft",
    bpf="bpf",
    pile_id="B-20",
)
print(f"{len(log.elevation)} logged feet, "
      f"from {log.elevation.max():.1f} to {log.elevation.min():.1f} ft")
```

The fines content comes from a second table of elevation versus percent
passing the No. 200 sieve. The mudline at this pile is 50 ft below datum,
32 ft above the first logged foot.

```{python}
fines = np.loadtxt("data/B-20_fines.csv", delimiter=",", skiprows=1)
soil = dp.SoilProfile(mudline=-50.0, elevation=fines[:, 0], fines=fines[:, 1])
```

## Stage 1: the capacity target

`prepare_target` applies the recalibrated Danish formula to each
foot, smooths the result with a Savitzky-Golay filter, anchors the final
foot to its unsmoothed value, and extends the grid up to the mudline.

```{python}
target = dp.prepare_target(log, soil)
print(f"grid of {len(target.elevation)} feet, {target.n_top} of them unlogged")
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: Formula capacity per foot (points) and the smoothed target (line).
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.5, 6))
ax.plot(target.raw_capacity, target.elevation, ".", color="gray", label="formula per foot")
ax.plot(target.capacity, target.elevation, color="C0", label="smoothed target")
ax.axhline(target.mudline, color="k", lw=0.8, ls="--")
ax.set_xlabel("capacity at time of driving (kips)")
ax.set_ylabel("elevation (ft)")
ax.legend(loc="lower left")
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```

## Stage 2: the unlogged top segment

The pile passed through 32 ft of soil before the inspector started
logging. `sweep_top_phi` assigns a constant friction angle to that segment,
runs the march for each value from 25 to 45 degrees, and records the
root-mean-square misfit between the modeled and target capacities over the
logged feet.

```{python}
band = dp.sweep_top_phi(target)
print(f"admissible top-segment friction angle: {band.lo:.0f} to {band.hi:.0f} deg")
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: Misfit of the march versus the assumed top-segment friction angle. The shaded range is the admissible band.
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5))
ax.plot(band.phi, band.rms, "o-")
ax.axvspan(band.lo, band.hi, color="C0", alpha=0.15)
ax.set_xlabel("top-segment friction angle (deg)")
ax.set_ylabel("RMS misfit (kips)")
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```

The log cannot distinguish between angles inside the band. The
deterministic analysis uses the lowest one; the Monte Carlo draws from the
whole band.

## Stage 3: the march

`run_drive` characterizes each logged foot from the toe resistance the
target demands after subtracting the shaft resistance of the feet above,
and tracks the pore pressure that later blows generate in every foot.

```{python}
result = dp.run_drive(target, top_phi=band.lo)
print(f"RMS misfit {result.rms_kips:.1f} kips")
print("outcome codes:", result.reason_counts())
print(f"{100 * result.fraction_liquefied():.0f}% of the logged feet liquefied during the drive")
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: Capacity target and the modeled capacity at the time of driving.
result.plot_fit()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: Friction angle, equivalent blow count and end-of-drive pore-pressure ratio. The dashed line is the top of the logged record.
result.plot_profile()
plt.show()
```

The per-foot arrays are plain NumPy arrays on the result:

```{python}
logged = result.logged
np.column_stack([
    result.elevation[logged][:8],
    result.phi[logged][:8].round(1),
    result.n160[logged][:8].round(0),
    result.felt[logged][:8].round(0),
    result.cycles_to_liq[logged][:8].round(0),
    result.ru[logged][:8].round(2),
])
```

## Stage 4: long-term capacity

The long-term capacity is the shaft resistance of every foot after its
pore pressure has dissipated plus the toe resistance at the end of the
drive. `long_term_capacity` returns the two parts; `run_drive` has already
stored them on the result.

```{python}
shaft, toe = dp.long_term_capacity(result)
print(f"end of drive  {result.eod_capacity:6.0f} kips")
print(f"long term     {result.ltc:6.0f} kips = shaft {shaft:.0f} + toe {toe:.0f}")
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: Unit shaft resistance at the end of the drive and after pore-pressure dissipation.
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.5, 6))
ax.plot(result.fs_eod, result.elevation, label="end of drive")
ax.plot(result.fs_ltc, result.elevation, label="long term")
ax.set_xlabel("unit shaft resistance (ksf)")
ax.set_ylabel("elevation (ft)")
ax.legend(loc="lower right")
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```

## Stage 5: Monte Carlo

`monte_carlo` repeats the march with the five uncertainty sources drawn
per realization. The target and the band computed above are passed in so
they are not recomputed. A seed makes the run reproducible; the
realization limit is lowered here to keep the page quick to build.

```{python}
mc_opts = dp.MonteCarloOptions(seed=1, chunk=50, max_realizations=200)
mc = dp.monte_carlo(log, soil, mc_options=mc_opts, target=target, top_band=band)
mean, half = mc.mean_ci()
q05, q50, q95 = mc.quantiles([0.05, 0.5, 0.95])
print(f"{mc.n} realizations, converged: {mc.converged}")
print(f"mean {mean:.0f} +/- {half:.0f} kips, median {q50:.0f}, 5th to 95th {q05:.0f} to {q95:.0f}")
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: Long-term capacity over the realizations, with the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles.
mc.plot_ltc()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: Friction angle percentiles per foot over the realizations.
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.5, 6))
p = mc.phi_quantiles
ax.fill_betweenx(mc.elevation, p[:, 0], p[:, 4], color="C0", alpha=0.2, label="5th to 95th")
ax.fill_betweenx(mc.elevation, p[:, 1], p[:, 3], color="C0", alpha=0.4, label="25th to 75th")
ax.plot(p[:, 2], mc.elevation, color="C0", label="median")
ax.set_xlabel("friction angle (deg)")
ax.set_ylabel("elevation (ft)")
ax.legend(loc="lower left")
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```

## The same in one call

`analyze` runs stages 1 to 4, and stage 5 when asked, and returns them
together.

```{python}
out = dp.analyze(log, soil)
print(out.drive.ltc == result.ltc, out.top_band.lo == band.lo)
```
